title: How to Sear Scallops
summary: Master the art of searing scallops to achieve a beautiful golden crust and tender, succulent interior with these straightforward steps.
body:
## How to Sear Scallops

There's something undeniably elegant about perfectly seared scallops. Their sweet, delicate flavor and tender texture, crowned with a beautiful golden-brown crust, can elevate any meal. Yet, many home cooks hesitate, fearing they'll end up with rubbery or bland results. The truth is, searing scallops is incredibly simple when you know a few key techniques. With Mise, we're here to guide you to culinary success, ensuring every scallop you cook is a triumph.

## The Secret to a Perfect Crust

The most crucial step for achieving that coveted golden crust begins before your scallops even touch the pan: **pat scallops completely dry: dry scallops sear, wet scallops steam.** This isn't just a suggestion; it's a fundamental rule. Any moisture on the surface of your scallops will cool the pan and prevent browning, leading to a steamed, rather than seared, texture. Use paper towels to thoroughly blot every side of each scallop until they feel almost tacky. This preparation is the bedrock of a successful sear.

Next, take a moment to inspect your scallops. You'll often find a small, tough, crescent-shaped muscle on the side of each scallop. This adductor muscle can be a bit chewy, so for the best eating experience, **remove the small side muscle before cooking.** It pulls off easily with your fingers and ensures your scallops are uniformly tender.

## Heating Your Pan Just Right

Choosing the right pan is important; a heavy-bottomed skillet, like cast iron or stainless steel, works wonders for even heat distribution. Add a neutral oil with a high smoke point, like grapeseed or canola, to your pan. The next critical step is to get the pan hot enough. You're looking for that sweet spot where the oil is ready to do its job without burning. **Heat the pan until the oil shimmers.** This visual cue tells you the pan has reached the ideal temperature for searing, creating an immediate, intense heat that will form that gorgeous crust.

## The Sear Itself: Patience is Key

Once your pan is shimmering hot, carefully place your dried, destringed scallops into the pan in a single layer, ensuring they're not overcrowded. Give them a little space so the pan doesn't cool down too much. Now, for the most challenging, yet vital, part: resist the urge to move them! **Don't move the scallops for 90 seconds to 2 minutes per side.** This undisturbed time allows the Maillard reaction—the browning that creates rich flavors and aromas—to occur fully, building that incredible crust. After the initial side, flip them gently and sear the other side for another 90 seconds to 2 minutes. The exact timing will depend on the size of your scallops and your desired doneness, but trust your eyes for a deep, golden-brown hue.

Your scallops are done when they're opaque throughout with that irresistible crust. Serve them immediately to enjoy their delicate flavor and perfect texture. With these simple techniques, you'll be searing scallops like a pro, impressing yourself and your guests every time.

title: Knife Skills: Dice, Mince and Julienne
summary: Mastering basic knife cuts like dicing, mincing, and julienning will not only make your cooking more efficient but also elevate the appearance and texture of your Mise meals.
body:
## Knife Skills: Dice, Mince and Julienne

Welcome to the heart of your kitchen success: knife skills! At Mise, we believe that confident knife work is the foundation for delicious and beautifully prepared meals. Don't be intimidated; with a little practice and the right techniques, you'll be slicing and dicing like a pro in no time, making your cooking journey safer and much more enjoyable.

## The Claw Grip: Your Safety First!

Before you make any cuts, let's talk safety. The most important technique for protecting your fingers is the "claw grip." To do this, simply tuck your fingertips behind your knuckles, creating a protective barrier with your knuckles against the knife blade. This positions your fingers out of harm's way while guiding the knife. Always keep your dominant hand on the knife handle, and your non-dominant hand forming the claw, holding the food securely. Practice this even with a dull knife to build muscle memory.

## Mastering the Dice

Dicing means cutting food into small, uniform cubes. Uniformity isn't just for looks; it ensures your ingredients cook evenly, leading to better flavor and texture in your dishes. Start by squaring off your ingredient, then cut it into even planks, then into sticks, and finally, into cubes. We often specify different dice sizes in our recipes:

*   A small dice is 1/4 inch
*   A medium dice is 1/2 inch
*   A large dice is 3/4 inch

Practicing these different sizes helps you achieve precision for various dishes, from delicate salsas to hearty stews.

## The Finer Art of Mincing

Mincing is about creating the smallest possible pieces of food, usually for aromatics like garlic, ginger, or herbs, to ensure their flavor disperses evenly throughout a dish without any large chunks. When an ingredient is minced, it means it's cut smaller than 1/8 inch. To mince, after dicing your ingredient very finely, you can gather the pieces and rock your knife back and forth over them repeatedly until they reach the desired super-fine consistency. The smaller the pieces, the more intense and evenly distributed the flavor will be.

## Elegant Julienne

Julienne is a classic French cut, known for its elegant, slender matchstick shape. This cut is perfect for vegetables that you want to cook quickly, add texture to salads, or use as a garnish. When we ask for julienne, we're looking for matchsticks that are 1/8 inch thick and about 2 inches long. To achieve this, first, square off your ingredient. Then, slice it into thin planks. Stack these planks, and then slice them lengthwise into uniform matchsticks. The uniform shape is key to both presentation and even cooking.

Practice makes perfect when it comes to knife skills. Start with softer vegetables like zucchini or potatoes, and gradually work your way up to harder ones. With these techniques in your toolkit, you'll prepare your Mise ingredients with confidence and create delicious meals every time.

title: Braising 101
summary: Master the art of braising to transform tough cuts of meat into incredibly tender, flavorful dishes with this simple guide.
body:
## Braising 101: Unlocking Deep Flavor with Mise

Welcome to Braising 101, Mise home cooks! Braising is a cooking technique that sounds fancy, but it's really all about slow, gentle cooking in a small amount of liquid. It's one of the most rewarding ways to cook, especially when you want to achieve incredibly tender meat that practically falls apart, all while building layers of rich, comforting flavor. It’s perfect for those busy days when you want to prep a meal and let your oven do the hard work, coming home to an amazing aroma and a delicious dinner.

## Choosing Your Cut

The magic of braising shines brightest with tougher cuts of meat. These are often more affordable and come packed with flavor, making them ideal candidates for this low-and-slow method. Think about cuts like chuck roast, beef short ribs, pork shoulder, or even lamb shanks. These cuts have connective tissue that, when cooked slowly with moisture, breaks down beautifully, leaving you with that melt-in-your-mouth tenderness we all crave.

## Building the Flavor Foundation

The first step to any great braise is building a strong flavor base. You’ll want to **brown the meat well before adding liquid**. This step is non-negotiable! Sear your chosen cut on all sides in a hot pot or Dutch oven until it develops a deep, rich brown crust. This browning creates complex flavors through something called the Maillard reaction, which adds incredible depth to your finished dish. Don’t rush this part; a good sear is worth the effort. Once browned, remove the meat from the pot.

Next, you can add some aromatic vegetables like onions, carrots, and celery to the same pot, softening them gently to create another layer of flavor. You might deglaze the pan with a splash of liquid, scraping up all those flavorful browned bits from the bottom – those are pure gold!

## The Perfect Braising Environment

Now it's time to bring it all together. Return your browned meat to the pot. Add your braising liquid, which could be broth, wine, or even crushed tomatoes, depending on your recipe. The crucial part here is the amount: **the liquid should come one-third to halfway up the meat**, but not completely submerge it. This allows part of the meat to steam while the submerged portion cooks in the liquid, ensuring an even, tender result. The liquid will transform into a luscious sauce as it cooks.

Once your liquid is in, put the lid on your pot. You’ll want to **braise covered in a 325°F oven**. The oven provides gentle, even heat from all directions, which is much better for braising than a stovetop, where the heat only comes from below. This consistent temperature is key to slowly breaking down those tough fibers.

## Patience is a Virtue

Braising isn't a quick sprint; it's a slow marathon. For tough cuts like chuck roast or short ribs, expect the cooking process to take **2 to 3 hours**. The exact timing can vary, so the best indicator of doneness is texture: the meat is done when it’s **fork-tender**. You should be able to easily pull it apart with just a fork. Resist the urge to rush it; that long, slow cook is what creates magic.

Once your braise is complete, remove it from the oven. For best results and even more tender meat, let it rest for a bit before serving. You can even skim any excess fat from the surface of the sauce if desired. The resulting dish will be incredibly rich, flavorful, and a testament to the power of slow cooking. Enjoy your delicious, home-cooked braised meal, courtesy of your skills and a little help from Mise!

title: Perfect Stovetop Rice
summary: Master the art of cooking perfect stovetop rice with these simple techniques and precise measurements for various types of rice.
body:
Perfect stovetop rice might seem like a simple task, but getting it just right – fluffy, separate grains every time – can feel like a culinary mystery. At Mise, we believe delicious meals start with perfect components, and rice is no exception. With a few simple steps and the right ratios, you'll be serving flawless rice that elevates any dish, from our delicious stir-fries to a comforting side for our roasted chicken.

## The Essential First Step: Rinsing

No matter what type of rice you're cooking, the very first step is often overlooked but incredibly important: rinsing. Rinsing your rice helps remove excess starch, which can make your cooked rice sticky and clumpy. Place your rice in a fine-mesh sieve or a bowl and rinse it under cold water, gently swirling it, until the water runs clear. This simple action makes a huge difference in the final texture.

## Mastering Long-Grain White Rice

This is a staple for many households, and achieving a light, fluffy texture is easier than you think. For long-grain white rice, the ideal ratio is 1 cup rice to 1 1/2 cups water. Combine the rinsed rice and water in a pot with a tight-fitting lid. Bring it to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer covered for 15 minutes. Absolutely resist the urge to peek during this time! Once the simmering is done, take the pot off the heat, keeping it covered, and let it rest off the heat for 10 minutes. Finally, fluff with a fork before serving.

## A Note on Jasmine Rice

Jasmine rice, known for its fragrant aroma and slightly sticky texture, is a favorite. While the cooking method is similar to long-grain white, the water ratio is slightly different to achieve its characteristic consistency. For Jasmine rice, use 1 cup rice to 1 1/4 cups water. Follow the same simmering and resting process as long-grain white for excellent results.

## Conquering Brown Rice

Brown rice is a fantastic whole grain option, offering a nuttier flavor and chewier texture. It requires a bit more water and a longer simmer time than white rice varieties. For brown rice, you'll need 1 cup rice to 2 cups water. Combine the rinsed brown rice and water in a pot, bring it to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes. After simmering, remove it from the heat and let it rest, covered, for another 10 minutes before fluffing and serving.

With these straightforward techniques and exact measurements, you'll be a stovetop rice master in no time. Enjoy perfectly cooked rice with your next Mise meal!

title: Make a Pan Sauce in Five Minutes
summary: Transform your weeknight meals with a restaurant-quality pan sauce made in just minutes, perfect for adding incredible flavor to any protein.
body:
## The Secret Weapon for Amazing Meals

You’ve just seared a beautiful piece of chicken, pork, or steak, and your pan is left with those delightful, crusty bits stuck to the bottom. Don’t wash them away! Those browned bits, known as "fond," are pure flavor gold, and they're the foundation for an incredible pan sauce that comes together surprisingly fast. Making a pan sauce is one of the easiest ways to elevate a simple meal from good to extraordinary, using ingredients you likely already have. It's a technique that truly transforms pan juices into a rich, savory companion for your main dish.

## What You'll Need

Creating a delicious pan sauce requires just a few simple additions to your pan after you’ve cooked your protein. You'll want a flavorful liquid, a little fat to finish, and a utensil for scraping. The beauty of this technique is its versatility; it works wonderfully with almost any seared meat or even hearty vegetables.

## From Searing to Sauce: The First Step

Once your protein is cooked and resting – giving it time to reabsorb its juices is key for tender results – you’re ready to begin the sauce. Leave any delicious drippings and browned bits in the pan. If there's too much excess oil, you can carefully pour some out, leaving just a thin coating.

## Deglaze for Deep Flavor

Now for the magic! Place your pan back on a burner over medium heat. Pour in **1/2 cup of wine or stock**. As the liquid hits the hot pan, it will start to bubble, releasing all those flavorful browned bits from the bottom. Grab a wooden spoon or a sturdy spatula and gently scrape up all the "fond." This isn't just about cleaning the pan; it's about incorporating every last speck of flavor into your developing sauce. Watch as the liquid transforms, taking on the rich color and taste of what you just cooked.

## Reduce and Concentrate

Let the liquid in the pan simmer gently. You want to cook it down until it has **reduced by half**. This process isn't just about reducing volume; it's about concentrating all those wonderful flavors. As the water evaporates, the essence of your ingredients intensifies, creating a more robust and flavorful sauce. Keep an eye on it – this step usually takes just a couple of moments.

## The Silky Finish

Once your sauce has reduced, take the pan **off the heat**. This is an important step to ensure the butter emulsifies correctly and doesn't separate. Now, add **1 tablespoon of cold butter** to the hot liquid. Swirl the pan gently, or whisk with a small whisk, until the butter melts and fully incorporates into the sauce. The cold butter helps to thicken the sauce slightly, adding a beautiful sheen and a luscious, velvety texture. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper to taste.

## Serve and Enjoy!

Immediately spoon your freshly made pan sauce over your rested protein, pasta, or even roasted vegetables. The rich, savory liquid will bring a burst of flavor to every bite. This simple, elegant technique shows how easy it is to create something truly special. With Mise, you're not just cooking meals; you're mastering techniques that make every dish a delight.

title: Toasting and Blooming Spices
summary: Elevate your cooking by learning the simple yet impactful techniques of toasting whole spices and blooming ground spices, bringing out their full flavor potential.
body:
## Toasting and Blooming Spices: Unlock Incredible Flavor
Many home cooks think of spices as just something to sprinkle into a dish. While that works, there are two simple techniques that will transform your cooking and unlock a whole new world of aromatic depth: toasting whole spices and blooming ground spices. These methods are easy to master and will make your Mise meals, and all your cooking, sing with vibrant flavor.

## Why Bother with Spices?
Spices aren't just for adding a bit of heat or color. They carry complex oils and compounds that contribute significantly to the taste, aroma, and even the texture of your food. When used correctly, spices can elevate a humble dish into something extraordinary. Think of a rich curry, a fragrant soup, or a zesty marinade—spices are often the secret heroes.

## The Magic of Toasting Whole Spices
Toasting whole spices is all about waking them up. When spices are whole and untoasted, their aromatic oils are locked inside. A quick toast in a dry pan gently heats these spices, causing their oils to release and their flavors to deepen and become more nuanced.

To achieve this, **toast whole spices in a dry pan for 1 to 2 minutes, until fragrant.** You'll know they're ready when you can smell their beautiful aroma filling your kitchen. Don't walk away! They can burn quickly. Once toasted, you can grind them for fresh spice blends or add them whole to dishes like stews and curries for slow-release flavor. This step adds an incredible depth that pre-ground, untoasted spices simply can't match.

## Blooming Ground Spices for Instant Impact
Blooming ground spices is a slightly different technique, but just as powerful. This involves briefly cooking ground spices in a small amount of hot oil or butter at the beginning of your cooking process. This quick sauté allows the spice compounds to dissolve into the fat, which then disperses those flavors throughout your entire dish more evenly and intensely.

For this technique, **bloom ground spices in hot oil for about 30 seconds.** The key here is not to burn them; keep the heat moderate and stir constantly. This process helps to smooth out any raw, harsh edges ground spices might have, making their flavor more mellow and integrated into the dish. It's especially wonderful for curries, dals, and any dish where spices form the flavor base.

## A Special Note on Asafoetida (Hing)
Asafoetida, often called "hing," is a fascinating and potent spice, particularly common in Indian cuisine. It offers a unique savory, onion-like, or garlic-like flavor, making it a fantastic addition or substitute in many dishes, especially for those who avoid alliums. Due to its intensity, a little goes a very long way.

When using this powerful spice, remember to **use only a pinch of asafoetida (hing).** It's often bloomed in hot oil with other spices to mellow its pungent raw aroma into something wonderfully savory. It's also important to note that **most asafoetida is cut with wheat flour, so it isn't gluten-free unless the label says so.** Always check the packaging if gluten is a concern for you or your diners.

## Elevate Your Everyday Cooking
Incorporating toasting and blooming into your cooking routine is a game-changer. These techniques are simple, don't require special equipment, and dramatically enhance the flavor profile of your meals. By taking these few extra moments, you'll unlock the true potential of your spice cabinet and bring restaurant-quality depth to your home kitchen. Get ready to experience your favorite recipes with newfound vibrancy and aroma!

title: Safe Internal Cooking Temperatures
summary: Ensuring your food reaches the correct internal temperature is crucial for delicious and safe meals.
body:
# Safe Internal Cooking Temperatures

Cooking at home is a rewarding experience, and at Mise, we want to help you make every meal not just delicious, but also perfectly safe. One of the most important tools in your kitchen arsenal for food safety is an instant-read thermometer. Using it correctly ensures that your dishes are cooked through, eliminating harmful bacteria and making sure your family enjoys every bite without worry.

## Why Temperature Matters

When you cook meat, poultry, fish, or eggs, heating them to a specific internal temperature kills bacteria that can cause foodborne illness. You can't always tell if food is safely cooked just by looking at its color or texture. That's why an instant-read thermometer is your best friend in the kitchen. It gives you an accurate reading, taking the guesswork out of cooking and giving you peace of mind.

## Essential Temperatures for Your Meals

Here's a handy guide to the safe internal temperatures for various foods. Always remember to check with an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the food, avoiding bones and fat.

### Poultry Perfection

For all poultry, including ground poultry like chicken or turkey burgers, you'll want to reach a temperature of 165°F (74°C). This ensures your chicken breasts, whole roasted birds, and ground poultry dishes are cooked to a safe standard.

### Ground Meats

When cooking ground beef, ground pork, or ground lamb, the safe internal temperature is 160°F (71°C). This applies to your meatloaf, meatballs, and any other dishes made with ground meats.

### Whole Cuts of Meat

For whole cuts of beef, pork, lamb, and veal, such as steaks, roasts, or chops, cook them to 145°F (63°C). Once they reach this temperature, it's important to then let them rest for 3 minutes before carving or serving. This resting period allows the juices to redistribute, making the meat more tender and flavorful, and also completes the cooking process safely.

### Fish and Shellfish

Delicate fish fillets and shellfish, like shrimp, scallops, or mussels, are safely cooked when they reach an internal temperature of 145°F (63°C). They will often become opaque and flake easily when ready.

### Egg Dishes

Egg dishes, like quiches, frittatas, or casseroles containing eggs, should be cooked to 160°F (71°C). For individual eggs, cook until the yolk and white are firm.

## Reheating Leftovers Safely

Enjoying leftovers is a great way to minimize waste and savor your delicious meals again. When reheating any leftovers, make sure they reach an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C). This ensures that any bacteria that might have grown during storage are eliminated. Always use your instant-read thermometer to confirm.

## Your Kitchen Confidant

An instant-read thermometer is a small investment that pays big dividends in food safety and cooking confidence. By following these simple temperature guidelines and always checking your food in the thickest part, you'll serve up safe, delicious meals every time. Happy cooking from your friends at Mise!

title: Storing Your Mise Box
summary: Ensure your delicious Mise ingredients stay fresh and safe by following our simple storage guidelines as soon as your box arrives.
body:
## Storing Your Mise Box: Keep it Fresh and Safe!

Hey Mise home cooks! We know you’re excited to dive into your next delicious meal, and we’re just as excited for you. To make sure every bite is as fresh and flavorful as possible, and to keep your kitchen safe, proper storage of your ingredients is key. Don't worry, it's super easy, and we're here to guide you through it.

## The Grand Unboxing: Don't Delay!

First things first: when your Mise box arrives, give it some immediate love. We pack everything with care to keep it cool during transit, but the sooner you get things put away, the better. Please **unpack your box within 2 hours of delivery.** This helps maintain the quality and safety of all your lovely ingredients, especially the chilled ones. Get those perishables into the fridge right away!

## Where Everything Goes

Once unpacked, sort your ingredients. Most items will go straight into your refrigerator to keep them cold and extend their freshness. Think of your fridge as the cozy home for proteins, dairy, and most produce. Some items, like onions, garlic, or certain root vegetables, might prefer a cool, dry pantry. Your recipe cards will often offer specific advice for each ingredient.

## Taking Care of Your Proteins

Proteins are the stars of many Mise meals, and they need a little extra attention. Proper handling ensures they’re safe and tasty for your culinary adventures.

*   **Seafood:** Fresh seafood is a delight! To enjoy it at its best and safest, plan to **cook seafood within 2 days of delivery.**
*   **Meat and Poultry:** For all other delicious cuts, like chicken, beef, pork, or lamb, please make sure to **cook meat and poultry within 3 days of delivery.**
*   **Freezing for Later:** Life gets busy, we get it! If your plans change and you find you won't be able to cook a protein within the recommended timeframe, no problem at all. Just be sure to **freeze it on delivery day** to preserve its quality and safety for a future meal. Freezing stops the clock on freshness!

## Keeping Your Produce Vibrant

Our fresh produce brings color and nutrition to your plate. To keep those veggies and fruits crisp and delicious, plan to **use produce within 5 days of delivery.** Store them in the crisper drawer of your fridge or as directed by your recipe card to maximize their shelf life.

## A Little Care Goes a Long Way

Following these simple storage tips will help you get the most out of every Mise box, ensuring your meals are always fresh, delicious, and safe. We're passionate about making home cooking enjoyable and worry-free, and good food safety practices are a big part of that. Happy cooking, and enjoy every bite!

title: Thawing Frozen Proteins Safely
summary: Ensure your Mise meal-kit proteins are ready for cooking safely and deliciously by following these essential thawing guidelines.
body:
## Thawing Frozen Proteins Safely: A Mise Guide

At Mise, we're all about making your cooking experience enjoyable and, most importantly, safe! When you receive delicious proteins in your meal kit, they often arrive frozen to lock in freshness. Thawing these ingredients correctly is a crucial step in preparing a fantastic meal and preventing foodborne illness. Let's explore the best ways to get your proteins ready for the pan, oven, or grill.

## The Safest Bet: Refrigerator Thawing

Thawing in the refrigerator is by far the safest and most recommended method. It allows your protein to thaw slowly and evenly, keeping it out of the "danger zone" where harmful bacteria can multiply rapidly. This method requires a bit of foresight, so it’s perfect for planning your next Mise meal. Simply place your frozen protein (still in its original packaging or a sealed container to prevent drips) on a plate or tray on the bottom shelf of your refrigerator. A good rule of thumb to remember is: Thaw in the fridge: allow about 24 hours for every 5 pounds. This ensures a thorough and safe thaw, allowing you to cook with confidence when you're ready.

## When Time is Ticking: Cold Water Thawing

If you're a bit pressed for time and need your protein thawed more quickly, cold water thawing is an excellent alternative. It's much faster than the refrigerator but still keeps your food at a safe temperature. For this method, it's absolutely essential to keep your protein sealed in a watertight bag. This prevents water from getting into the food and bacterial cross-contamination. Submerge the sealed package in a bowl of cold tap water. The key to effective and safe cold water thawing is constant cold. Make sure to change the water every 30 minutes to keep it cold and ensure the thawing process continues efficiently. Once thawed, cook the protein immediately.

## For the Instant Cook: Microwave Thawing

Sometimes you realize you forgot to thaw your protein until the very last minute – it happens to the best of us! Your microwave can come to the rescue for a super-speedy thaw. Most microwaves have a defrost setting that cycles on and off to prevent the food from cooking. While convenient, this method often begins to cook the edges of the food, so it's not ideal for all proteins or for food you plan to refrigerate later. Because parts of the food may start to cook during microwave thawing, it's critical to Cook food immediately after thawing it in the microwave. Do not refreeze protein thawed this way, and always ensure it's cooked to the proper internal temperature right away.

## A Crucial Warning: What to Avoid

While there are safe and effective ways to thaw your Mise proteins, there are also methods that pose serious health risks and should always be avoided. The most important rule to remember for food safety is: Never thaw meat or fish on the counter. Leaving frozen protein out at room temperature allows the outer layers to warm up and enter the "danger zone" (temperatures between 40°F and 140°F) where bacteria can multiply rapidly, even if the center is still frozen. This applies to thawing in hot water as well – it's just not safe. Always use one of the approved methods to protect yourself and your loved ones from foodborne illness.

By following these simple guidelines, you can confidently prepare and enjoy every meal from your Mise kit, knowing your ingredients have been handled safely from start to finish. Happy cooking!

title: Common Ingredient Substitutions
summary: Discover easy and practical ingredient substitutions to keep your cooking smooth and stress-free, even when you're missing an item.
body:
Ever find yourself halfway through a recipe only to realize you're missing a key ingredient? Don't panic! Being a confident home cook often means knowing how to adapt. At Mise, we believe cooking should be enjoyable and stress-free, which is why we've put together a handy guide to common ingredient substitutions. These clever swaps will save you a trip to the grocery store and keep your cooking adventures on track.

## Dairy Swaps

Dairy ingredients are often essential for moisture and richness. If you're out of stock or have dietary preferences, these swaps are lifesavers.

**Buttermilk:** If a recipe calls for buttermilk, it's easy to make your own. Combine 1 cup milk with 1 tablespoon lemon juice or vinegar. Stir and let it rest for 5 minutes. It will curdle slightly, creating a perfect substitute. This works wonderfully in pancakes and biscuits.

**Sour Cream and Greek Yogurt:** For a healthy and often thicker alternative to sour cream, plain Greek yogurt is excellent. These two can swap 1:1 in most recipes, from dollops on chili to creamy dips and baked goods. Greek yogurt offers a similar tang and rich texture.

## Egg Alternatives

Eggs play many roles in cooking. If you're out or prefer an egg-free option, there's a popular plant-based swap.

**Flax Egg:** For recipes where an egg acts as a binder, a 'flax egg' is fantastic. To make one, mix 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed with 3 tablespoons water. Let this mixture rest for 5 minutes until it thickens. This substitute works well in muffins and cookies.

## Flavor Enhancers

Herbs and sauces bring distinct flavors. Knowing how to swap them effectively can make all the difference.

**Fresh vs. Dried Herbs:** While fresh herbs offer vibrant flavor, dried herbs are a convenient pantry staple. The general rule for substituting is straightforward: 1 tablespoon of fresh herbs equals 1 teaspoon of dried herbs. Dried herbs are more concentrated, so use less.

**Soy Sauce Alternatives:** For those with dietary restrictions, soy sauce has excellent alternatives. Swap soy sauce for tamari to make a dish gluten-free. For a soy-free option, you can use coconut aminos. Coconut aminos are a dark, salty, and slightly sweet sauce from coconut blossoms, great for soy-free and gluten-free diets.

## Conclusion

With these simple swaps in your culinary toolkit, you’ll be ready for almost anything your recipes throw your way. Don't let a missing ingredient stop you from creating delicious meals. Happy cooking from your friends at Mise!

title: Dairy-Free Swaps
summary: Discover easy and delicious dairy-free substitutions to make your Mise meals work for any dietary preference.
body:
## Dairy-Free Swaps for Delicious Mise Meals

At Mise, we believe everyone should enjoy delicious home-cooked meals, regardless of dietary preferences. If you're looking to reduce your dairy intake or have a dairy allergy, adapting your favorite recipes doesn't have to be complicated. With a few simple swaps, you can transform many dishes into dairy-free delights without sacrificing flavor or texture. We've put together some of our favorite easy substitutions to help you get started on your culinary journey.

### Butter Alternatives

Butter is a staple in many kitchens, adding richness and flavor. But what do you do when you need a dairy-free option? We have two fantastic alternatives for you. When sautéing vegetables or making a savory sauce, you can replace butter with olive oil, using 3/4 of the amount specified in the recipe. Olive oil brings its own distinct flavor profile and healthy fats. If you prefer a more neutral taste or are baking, vegan butter is a perfect choice. You can replace butter with vegan butter 1:1, meaning you use the exact same quantity. These options ensure your dishes retain that comforting, rich quality you love.

### Creamy Goodness Without Dairy

Many recipes call for cream to add a luxurious, smooth texture to sauces, soups, and desserts. For a fantastic dairy-free alternative that delivers on creaminess, look no further than full-fat coconut milk. Its rich consistency and subtle sweetness make it an ideal replacement. Simply replace cream with full-fat coconut milk in your recipes. Don't worry about an overpowering coconut flavor; it often blends seamlessly, especially in savory dishes, adding depth without taking over. It's a wonderful way to achieve that velvety mouthfeel without any dairy.

### The Cheesy Flavor Secret: Nutritional Yeast

Missing that distinct, savory, umami flavor that grated parmesan brings? We've got a secret ingredient that's a game-changer for dairy-free cooking: nutritional yeast. Often called "nooch," it offers a cheesy, nutty taste that can seriously enhance your dishes. It's especially great for sprinkling over pasta, stirring into sauces, or even making dairy-free "cheese" sauces. As a general guide, to achieve a similar cheesy essence, you can replace 1/4 cup of grated parmesan with 2 tablespoons of nutritional yeast. Experiment with it; you might be surprised by how versatile and flavorful it is!

### Milk Made Easy

From creamy sauces to baking, milk is a foundational ingredient in countless recipes. For a straightforward dairy-free swap, unsweetened oat milk is a fantastic choice. It has a neutral flavor and a creamy texture that mimics dairy milk very well, making it incredibly versatile. Whether you're making a béchamel sauce, adding it to your morning oatmeal, or using it in a cake mix, you can easily replace milk with unsweetened oat milk 1:1. This means if a recipe calls for one cup of milk, you use one cup of unsweetened oat milk. It's a simple, effective, and delicious way to keep your meals dairy-free.

Embracing dairy-free cooking is easier than you think with these simple substitutions. Enjoy experimenting with these alternatives in your next Mise meal and discover a world of delicious possibilities!

title: Gluten-Free Swaps
summary: Easily adapt your favorite Mise recipes to be gluten-free with these simple and delicious substitution tips.
body:
Eating gluten-free doesn't mean sacrificing flavor or variety in your home cooking! Here at Mise, we believe everyone should enjoy delicious meals, and with a few smart swaps, you can easily adapt many recipes to fit a gluten-free lifestyle. Whether you're new to gluten-free cooking or just looking for some fresh ideas, these straightforward substitutions will help you create amazing dishes with confidence.

## Pasta Perfection

Love a comforting pasta dish? You don't have to give it up! For delicious gluten-free pasta dishes, reach for rice or chickpea pasta. These alternatives offer a great texture and soak up sauces beautifully. A helpful tip for achieving the perfect texture is to cook it 1 to 2 minutes less than the package says. This small adjustment helps prevent it from becoming too soft or gummy, ensuring you get that satisfying al dente bite every time. Enjoy your favorite Italian-inspired meals, completely gluten-free.

## Saucy Solutions

Many recipes call for flour as a thickener, especially in gravies, stews, and creamy sauces. But if you're avoiding gluten, cornstarch is your best friend! To thicken a sauce, 1 tablespoon of cornstarch replaces 2 tablespoons of flour. It's incredibly effective, so a little goes a long way. Always mix cornstarch with a small amount of cold water first to create a slurry before adding it to your hot liquid to prevent lumps. This trick will give you smooth, rich sauces without any gluten.

## Crumbly Comfort

Breadcrumbs are often used to add crunch, bind ingredients, or create a crispy topping. When a recipe calls for them, you can easily replace breadcrumbs with gluten-free panko or crushed rice crackers. Gluten-free panko offers that classic light, airy crunch, perfect for coating chicken or fish, or topping casseroles. Crushed rice crackers provide a similar texture and are excellent for binding meatballs or adding a savory element to gratins. Experiment with these options to keep that satisfying texture in all your dishes.

## Label Lookout

Sometimes, gluten can hide in unexpected places. It's always a good idea to check product labels, especially for ingredients that might surprise you. Keep an eye out because soy sauce, gochujang and most asafoetida contain wheat. But don't worry! The good news is that many brands now offer gluten-free versions of these staple ingredients. You can find gluten-free tamari (a soy sauce alternative), gluten-free gochujang, and pure asafoetida without wheat fillers. A quick check of the label ensures your meal stays completely gluten-free without compromising on flavor.

With these simple swaps, you can confidently navigate your kitchen and enjoy all your favorite Mise meals, tailored to your gluten-free needs. Happy cooking!

title: Missing or Damaged Ingredients: How Credits Work
summary: Learn how Mise handles missing or damaged ingredients, ensuring you get fair credit for any issues with your meal kit.
body:
## Missing or Damaged Ingredients: How Credits Work

We understand that sometimes things don't go exactly as planned. At Mise, we're committed to making sure your meal-kit experience is always a delight, and that includes promptly addressing any issues with your ingredients. If an ingredient is missing from your box or arrives damaged, don't worry – getting a credit is simple and straightforward.

## Reporting an Issue

If you notice a problem with an ingredient, please report it within 7 days of your delivery. The sooner you let us know, the faster we can help resolve the issue. To report, simply log into your Mise account, go to your order history, and select the box with the problem. You'll find an option there to report missing or damaged items. We only ask for a photo when an item arrived damaged, as this helps us understand what went wrong and improve our packaging. For missing items, a photo isn't needed.

## Understanding Your Credit

When an ingredient is missing or damaged, we provide a credit to your account. The credit equals the affected recipe's per-serving price times the servings in your plan. This ensures you're fairly compensated for the portion of the meal that was impacted. For example, if a key ingredient for a two-serving recipe is missing, and that recipe costs "X" per serving, you'll receive "2X" in credit. It's important to note that there are no cash refunds for missing ingredients; all compensation is provided as a credit to your Mise account.

## How Credits Are Approved

We aim to make the credit process as quick and easy as possible. Credits up to $25 per box are approved automatically. This means if the value of your missing or damaged ingredients falls within this amount for a single box, your credit will be applied almost instantly. For anything above $25 per box, the request is reviewed by our dedicated support team. We promise to review these larger requests within 1 business day, and we'll be in touch with you shortly after to confirm the credit.

## Using Your Credit

Once approved, your credits are automatically applied to your next box. There's no need to manually redeem them – they'll simply reduce the total cost of your upcoming order. And here's some good news: your credits never expire! So, even if you skip a week or two, your credit will be waiting for you when you're ready to order again.

We truly appreciate your understanding and patience. Our goal is always to deliver delicious, fresh ingredients right to your door, and we're here to help if anything ever falls short of that promise.

title: Skipping a Week or Pausing Your Subscription
summary: Learn how to easily manage your Mise subscription by skipping a week or pausing it entirely to fit your schedule.
body:
## Skipping a Week or Pausing Your Mise Subscription

Life happens, and sometimes you need flexibility with your meal kit delivery! At Mise, we make it simple to adjust your subscription so you only receive boxes when you're ready to cook. Whether you're going on vacation, have a busy week ahead, or just need a break, you have full control over your deliveries.

## How to Skip a Week

Skipping a week is a great option if you know you won't be around or able to cook for just a short period. It's easy to do directly from your account.

1. **Log In**: Head to your Mise account online.
2. **Navigate to "Upcoming Deliveries"**: Here you'll see a calendar view of your upcoming boxes.
3. **Select the Week to Skip**: Click on the specific week you want to skip.
4. **Confirm**: Follow the prompts to confirm your skip.

Remember, the weekly cutoff to skip a box is **Wednesday at 11:59 PM Pacific** for the following week's box. This means if you want to skip a box that's scheduled for delivery the next week, you need to make that change before Wednesday 11:59 PM Pacific. After this cutoff, your box is already being packed with fresh ingredients and can't be skipped. You can skip any week up to **8 weeks ahead**, giving you plenty of time to plan!

## How to Pause Your Subscription

If you need a longer break from Mise, pausing your subscription might be the best choice. This puts your deliveries on hold for a specified period, and your subscription will automatically resume afterward.

1. **Log In**: Access your account.
2. **Go to "Subscription Settings"**: You'll usually find this under your profile or account management section.
3. **Choose "Pause Subscription"**: Select this option.
4. **Set Your Pause Duration**: You can pause your subscription for **1 to 8 weeks**. Just pick the number of weeks that works for you.
5. **Confirm**: Confirm your pause, and we'll send you a reminder before your deliveries resume.

Remember, just like skipping a week, if you decide to pause your subscription after the **Wednesday at 11:59 PM Pacific** cutoff for the upcoming week's box, that particular box will still be delivered as it's already being prepared. Your pause will then take effect for subsequent weeks.

We hope this helps you manage your Mise subscription with ease! Our goal is to make healthy, delicious cooking accessible and flexible for your lifestyle. If you have any questions, our customer support team is always here to help.

title: Allergens at Mise
summary: Learn how Mise handles allergens, the precautions we take, and how you can manage your dietary needs with our meal kits.
body:
## Understanding Allergens at Mise

At Mise, we believe everyone should enjoy delicious, home-cooked meals. We understand that managing food allergies is a critical part of a healthy diet, and we want to be transparent about how we handle allergens in our kitchens and with our ingredients.

### Our Kitchen Environment and Allergen Handling

Your safety and peace of mind are very important to us. We want to inform you that **Mise kitchens handle all 9 major allergens: milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soy and sesame.** This means that while we take precautions, these ingredients are regularly present in our preparation areas.

Furthermore, it's important to know that **ingredients are packed in a shared facility, so cross-contact is possible.** We make every effort to prevent cross-contamination by following strict cleaning protocols and best practices in food handling. However, due to the nature of our operations and the shared environment, we must be clear that **we cannot guarantee that any recipe is allergen-free.** This is a crucial point for anyone with allergies to consider.

### How Mise Helps You Manage Your Allergies

We've built features into our service to help you navigate your dietary needs.

First, for each and every meal kit you receive, **every recipe card lists its allergens.** You'll find this information clearly marked on the physical card that comes with your delivery, as well as on the digital recipe available on our website and app. We encourage you to always review these details carefully before cooking.

Second, we've made it easy to customize your menu. You can **set your allergies in your preferences to hide recipes that contain them from your menu.** This personalized filtering tool allows you to browse your weekly options with greater confidence, knowing that recipes matching your specified allergens won't be shown to you. It's a great way to streamline your meal planning and focus on suitable dishes.

### Important Advice for Severe Allergies

While Mise provides tools and information to assist you, we strongly recommend a cautious approach for those with severe allergies. **Customers with severe allergies should talk to their doctor** or a healthcare professional before consuming our meal kits. They can provide personalized advice based on your specific health needs and the severity of your allergic reactions. Your health is paramount, and professional medical guidance is always the best resource for severe conditions.

We are committed to providing delicious and convenient meal solutions while being transparent about our allergen practices. We hope this information helps you make informed choices when enjoying Mise.
